building: Virginia C. Meredith Residence Hall South

criteria.name: Identity and provenance
evidence: Official Purdue BuildingShapes snapshot audit/official_purdue_buildings_wgs84.json has FID 410, BLDG_ABBR MRDS, BUILDING_N Virginia C. Meredith Residence Hall South, and address 1225 1st Street.
The official Purdue emergency plan names MRDS and gives 1225 1st Street; the MSKTD project page independently names Meredith South at Purdue.
deductions: The GIS source is a map feature, not survey control. The official facade image has no stated capture date.

criteria.name: Plan geometry and placement
evidence: Freshly opened asset in Blender 5.2.3; eight objects present in Asset_massing_meredith_hall_south_ffbc444.

The recorded transformed FID 410 perimeter extents and wall-shell extents differ by at most 0.000022 m on their axis-aligned bounds; the preview has the same long, articulated linear footprint character.
deductions: Only bounds were independently checked here, not a full vertex-by-vertex polygon overlay or master placement marker. The campus conversion is explicitly approximate and GIS positional accuracy is unpublished.

criteria.name: Exterior silhouette and openings
evidence: The single available official Purdue photo shows a long brick facade with articulated height/volume, prominent multi-story glazed vertical bays, and a highly glazed ground floor.
Mackey Mitchell’s architect page describes extensive ground-floor glass and retail dining at the east end (https://www.mackeymitchell.com/projects/meredith-residence-hall-south/).
Purdue’s current emergency plan says the hall has three sections: west A has eight floors; middle B and east C each have six floors (https://www.purdue.edu/operations/emergency-preparedness/mrds/).
deductions: The saved preview presents a mostly continuous six-band window grid and near-uniform roof height; it does not visibly express the documented eight-floor west A section versus six-floor B/C sections.
The large glass stair/study bays shown in the official photo are absent or only weakly represented by narrow end strips in the render.
The broad glazed and retail ground-floor frontage described by the architect is not modeled; windows remain small repeated punched openings down to grade.
Only one oblique exterior view is available, so other elevations and roofline transitions remain unchecked.

criteria.name: Materials and facade
evidence: The preview conveys brick, pale trim and blue-gray glazing; material slots are present on the eight mesh objects.
The official Purdue image shows dark red-brown masonry, dark framing, brighter glazing, and high-contrast glazed volumes.
deductions: The preview renders brick unusually pale/pink and flat compared with the source image; no close-up or material calibration image is available.
Facade bay rhythm and ground-floor glazing are materially more uniform and less articulated than the official source.

criteria.name: Interior / cutaway
evidence: The current asset is explicitly exterior-focused and the current preview is an exterior view.
deductions: No interior or cutaway is present in the opened asset; this criterion is therefore essentially unmet.

criteria.name: Presentation and technical quality
evidence: The exact saved .blend reopened in Blender 5.2.3 and contains the expected eight-object export collection.
Referenced texture paths are relative and resolve from the project root to materials/textures/red_brick/.
deductions: The only supplied review render is one oblique exterior view.

BMesh inspection found open/non-manifold boundaries on the wall shell (120 edges), parapet (120), and one-face roof slab (30); these may be intentional shell surfaces, but they are not closed solids and should be documented/checked for cutaway or downstream use.
The file-backed image records reported has_data=false on fresh open; their paths resolve, but actual texture image loading/use was not verified.

reviewed_views: Direct visual inspection of the official Purdue photo embedded in audit/meredith_hall/sources/purdue_conference_accommodations.html, labeled MEREDITH SOUTH RESIDENCE HALL – MSKTD

evidence_sources.provider: Purdue University Office of Emergency Preparedness
evidence_sources.inspected_claim: Page revision 2026-10-16; three sections, A west=8 floors; B middle=6 with basement; C east=6; two retail food operations on the first floor of east/C.

evidence_sources.provider: Mackey Mitchell Architects (project architect; MSKTD architect of record)
evidence_sources.inspected_claim: Ground floor has ample glass; retail dining venues at east end; 202,000 square feet.
Embedded photo of Meredith South labeled MSKTD; capture date unstated.
Large expanses of ground-floor glass and 730-bed program.

Coordinator reports this is the same exterior photograph embedded in Purdue Residences’ accommodations page. Treated as qualitative corroboration only; direct image fetch timed out during review, so the Corvias host/metadata were not independently verified.

findings.finding: Model reads as a uniform six-floor block; Purdue emergency plan documents eight floors in west A and six in middle B and east C.
findings.required_correction: Model the 8/6/6 section-height changes and verify their orientation against plan or imagery.

findings.finding: The documented glassy public base and east-end food retail are not represented in the saved preview.
findings.required_correction: Add broad ground-floor glazing and distinguish the east-end retail frontage.

findings.finding: Official photo shows multiple tall, multi-story glazed volumes that are missing or too weakly expressed in the current render.
findings.required_correction: Model prominent glazed vertical bays and their frame divisions from source imagery.

findings.finding: Repeated small windows and pale brick flatten the facade rhythm and color compared with the source photo.
findings.required_correction: Adjust window dimensions/spacing and brick value; retain unknown elevations as unverified until sourced.

uncertainties: Only one official exterior photo was inspected; hidden/rear elevations and roof equipment are not verified.
The photo capture date is not stated; architect and Purdue text corroborate the program but do not supply elevations.
GIS plan positional accuracy and the local geographic conversion error are unknown.
The shell’s open mesh boundaries may be deliberate massing surfaces; no solid-volume requirement was available.
No interior evidence was inspected and none is modeled.
The master blend and its placement for this asset were not reviewed.

The coordinator identified the inspected Purdue-embedded photo as matching a Corvias-hosted image URL; direct fetch of that URL timed out, so its Corvias publication context and metadata were not independently verified.
